literal: The emperor said: "This is not for me to know; it should be decided by you, the lords of the state."
idiomatic: The emperor said, "That is not for me to decide—it belongs to you, the lords of the realm."

literal: It happened that word came that Emperor Wu of Song had died; the emperor wished to take Luoyang, Wulao, and Huatai.
idiomatic: When news arrived that Emperor Wu of Song had died, the emperor wanted to seize Luoyang, Wulao, and Huatai.

literal: Hao said: "Your Majesty, though Liu Yu rose suddenly, received his envoys and tribute, and Yu also honored Your Majesty.
idiomatic: Hao said, "Your Majesty accepted Liu Yu when he rose abruptly, received his tribute, and Liu Yu in turn honored the throne."

literal: Now that he has unfortunately died, to attack while they mourn, though you might gain territory, would not be proper.
idiomatic: "Now that he is dead, to invade in their hour of mourning might win ground but would not be honorable."

literal: In the Spring and Autumn Annals, Jin's Shi Gai invaded Qi; hearing the Marquis of Qi had died, he turned back.
idiomatic: "The Spring and Autumn Annals records how Shi Gai of Jin invaded Qi but turned back on hearing the marquis had died."

literal: The noble man praised his not attacking during mourning, holding that such grace could move filial sons and such righteousness could stir the feudal lords.
idiomatic: "The noble man praised refusing to strike a house in mourning—grace enough to touch filial sons, righteousness enough to move the feudal lords."

literal: Now the state cannot settle the south in one stroke; you should send men to mourn and offer relief for their calamity, spreading righteous renown through the realm—a deed of commanding virtue.
idiomatic: "The realm cannot conquer the south in a single campaign. Send envoys to mourn, succor their disaster, and spread righteous fame under heaven—that is the deed of a ruler of commanding virtue."

literal: Moreover, with Yu newly dead, his faction has not yet dispersed; better to wait until their evil ripens.
idiomatic: "Moreover, Liu Yu is newly dead and his faction not yet split apart. Better to wait until their wickedness ripens."

literal: If powerful ministers contend for power, trouble will surely arise; then you may command generals to display might and take the lands north of the Huai without tiring the troops.
idiomatic: "If powerful ministers fight for power, crisis will follow. Then send generals to show force and take the Huai north without exhausting the army."

literal: " The emperor was keen on a southern campaign and said to Hao: "Liu Yu destroyed Yao Xing's state because Yao Xing died.
idiomatic: The emperor was set on war in the south and told Hao, "Liu Yu destroyed Yao Xing's state when Yao Xing died."

literal: Yu is dead—why may I not attack!"
idiomatic: "Liu Yu is dead—why should I not attack?"

literal: Hao stubbornly said: "When Xing died, his two sons fought each other—only then did Yu attack."
idiomatic: Hao held firm: "Yao Xing died and his two sons fought each other—only then did Liu Yu attack."

literal: The emperor was greatly angered and would not listen.
idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage and would not heed him.

literal: He then sent Xi Jin and others south, and before the heir apparent's court they debated: "Attack cities first, or seize territory first?"
idiomatic: He sent Xi Jin and others south. Before the heir apparent's court they debated whether to take cities first or overrun territory first.

literal: Jin asked to attack cities first.
idiomatic: Xi Jin asked to attack the cities first.

literal: Hao said: "Southerners excel at stubborn defense; Fu Jian's attack on Xiangyang took more than a year without success.
idiomatic: Hao said, "Southerners excel at stubborn defense. Fu Jian's siege of Xiangyang dragged on more than a year without success."

literal: Now with the great state's strength to attack their small cities, if you do not take them quickly, you will blunt the army's momentum—a perilous course.
idiomatic: "With the full strength of the empire against their small towns, failure to take them quickly will blunt the army's momentum—a dangerous course."

literal: Better to divide the army to overrun territory, taking the Huai as the limit, setting governors and magistrates to gather rent and grain.
idiomatic: "Better to divide the army and overrun territory up to the Huai, posting governors and magistrates to collect rent and grain."

literal: Huatai and Wulao would lie north of the army; cut off from southern rescue, they would surely flee east along the river.
idiomatic: "Huatai and Wulao would lie north of our forces, cut off from southern relief, and would surely flee east along the river."

literal: If not, they would be game within an enclosure."
idiomatic: "Otherwise they would be beasts inside a pen."

literal: Gongsun Biao asked to take their cities first.
idiomatic: Gongsun Biao urged attacking the cities first.

literal: Jin and the others crossed the river and first attacked Huatai; after a long time without success, Biao asked for reinforcements.
idiomatic: Xi Jin crossed the river and attacked Huatai first. After a long stalemate, Gongsun Biao asked for reinforcements.

literal: The emperor was angry and personally toured south, appointing Hao Governor of Xiangzhou and chief strategist with the army.
idiomatic: The emperor, enraged, marched south in person, made Hao governor of Xiangzhou, and kept him as chief strategist with the army.

literal: When the imperial carriage returned, Hao accompanied him to Xihe and Taiyuan, descended to view the river, and gazed at the towns along the banks, moved to deep feeling.
idiomatic: When the imperial train returned, Hao accompanied the tour to Xihe and Taiyuan, stood above the river, looked along the towns on its banks, and was stirred to deep reflection.

literal: He then debated with colleagues the rights and wrongs of the five ranks and commanderies and counties, examining the errors of the First Emperor of Qin and Emperor Wu of Han.
idiomatic: He then debated with colleagues the merits of restoring the five ranks of nobility versus the commandery-county system, weighing the failures of the First Emperor of Qin and Emperor Wu of Han.

literal: At the time all respected his words.
idiomatic: At the time all were impressed by his argument.

literal: The Celestial Master Kou Qianzhi often spoke with Hao; hearing his discourse on the rise and fall of antiquity, he would stay from night till dawn, straightening his manner and composing his face, deeply admiring him, and say: "This man's words are beneficent and all can be carried out; he is a Gao Yao for our age.
idiomatic: The Celestial Master Kou Qianzhi often talked with Hao. Hearing him trace the rise and fall of past ages, Kou would sit from night till dawn, rapt and composed, and say in deep admiration, "This man's words are beneficent and can all be put into practice. He is a Gao Yao for our age."

literal: Only men prize what is distant and slight what is near, and cannot examine him deeply."
idiomatic: "Only men prize what is far away and slight what is close at hand, and fail to study him deeply."

literal: He then said to Hao: "I shall embrace both Ru and teaching, assist the Perfect Lord of Great Peace, yet my learning does not examine antiquity.
idiomatic: He then told Hao, "I mean to embrace both Confucian teaching and the Way, to assist the Perfect Lord of Great Peace, yet my learning does not reach back to antiquity."

literal: Compose for me the political canons of successive kings and discuss their main points."
idiomatic: "Compose for me the political canons of successive kings and set out their main themes."

literal: Hao then wrote more than twenty chapters, reaching back to the Grand Beginning and down through the traces of Qin and Han change and decay, the great theme first taking restoration of the five ranks as its root.
idiomatic: Hao wrote more than twenty chapters, reaching from the Grand Beginning down through the rise and fall of Qin and Han, with restoration of the five ranks as the central theme.

literal: Emperor Taiwu's attendants, resenting Hao's uprightness, jointly slandered him.
idiomatic: Those about Emperor Taiwu, resenting Hao's uprightness, joined in slandering him.

literal: Though the emperor knew his ability, he could not escape the clamor of the multitude; therefore Hao was sent home on his noble title.
idiomatic: Though the emperor knew his talent, he could not defy the crowd's clamor, and Hao was sent home while retaining his noble title.

literal: When doubts arose, he was summoned to be questioned.
idiomatic: Whenever doubts arose, he was summoned for counsel.

literal: Hao was slender, fair, and white as a beautiful woman.
idiomatic: Hao was slight, fair-skinned, and delicate as a beautiful woman.

literal: By nature quick and penetrating, skilled in stratagem, he compared himself to Zhang Liang and said his mastery of antiquity surpassed Zhang's.
idiomatic: Quick and penetrating by nature, skilled in stratagem, he likened himself to Zhang Liang and claimed his command of antiquity surpassed Zhang's.

literal: After returning home, he wished to practice ingestion and nourishing life; Kou Qianzhi had the Scripture of the Divine Central Record and New Classic, and Hao therefore took him as master.
idiomatic: Back at home he wished to practice dietetics and longevity arts. Kou Qianzhi possessed the Scripture of the Divine Central Record and New Classic, and Hao became his disciple.

literal: In the Shiguang era he was advanced to Duke of Dongjun and appointed Minister of Ceremonies.
idiomatic: In the Shiguang era he was raised to Duke of Dongjun and made Minister of Ceremonies.

literal: At the time they debated attacking Helian Chang; the ministers all thought it difficult, but only Hao said: "In years past Mars twice held the Feathered Forest and crossed the Hooked Array—its omen is the fall of Qin.
idiomatic: When the court debated attacking Helian Chang, every minister called it hard—only Hao said, "For years Mars twice held the Feathered Forest and crossed the Hooked Array—an omen of Qin's fall."

literal: Moreover this year the five planets all appear in the east, favorable to a western campaign.
idiomatic: "This year the five planets all stand in the east, favoring a western campaign."

literal: Heaven answers man and the seasons converge—one must advance."
idiomatic: "Heaven answers man, the seasons converge—you must advance."

literal: The emperor then sent Xi Jin and others to strike Puban while he personally led light cavalry to raid their capital, returning with great booty.
idiomatic: The emperor sent Xi Jin and others against Puban while he personally led light cavalry to raid their capital and returned with great booty.

literal: Later he campaigned against Chang again, halting below his walls and gathering troops in a feigned retreat.
idiomatic: Later he attacked Chang again, halted below his walls, and feigned a withdrawal.

literal: Chang advanced with drums and shouts, spreading his array in two wings.
idiomatic: Chang advanced with drums and shouts and spread his line into two wings.

literal: Wind and rain came from the southeast, raising sand and darkening the sky; the eunuch Zhao Ni stepped forward and said: "Now wind and rain come from behind the enemy; we face their backs—Heaven does not help us.
idiomatic: Wind and rain came from the southeast, whipping sand until the sky went dark. The eunuch Zhao Ni stepped forward and said, "The storm comes from behind the enemy while we face their backs—Heaven is not with us."

literal: Moreover the officers and men are hungry and thirsty; I beg Your Majesty to gather the cavalry and withdraw, and wait for another day."
idiomatic: "The troops are hungry and thirsty. I beg Your Majesty to gather the cavalry and withdraw until another day."

literal: Hao shouted at him: "What words are these!"
idiomatic: Hao shouted him down: "What talk is this!"

literal: To win a thousand li away, within a single day—how can you change plans?
idiomatic: "Victory a thousand li away cannot be thrown away in a single day—how can plans be changed?"

literal: The enemy advances without stopping and their rear is already cut off; you should divide the army to hide in the hills and strike them unawares.
idiomatic: "The enemy presses on without pause and their rear is already cut off. Divide the army, hide in the hills, and strike them unawares."

literal: The way of wind lies with men—how could it be constant?"
idiomatic: "Wind serves those who use it—how could it be constant?"

literal: The emperor said: "Good."
idiomatic: The emperor said, "Well said."

literal: Dividing the cavalry they struck fiercely and Chang's army collapsed in great rout.
idiomatic: They split the cavalry, struck hard, and Chang's army collapsed in rout.

literal: In the second year of Shenjue they debated striking the Rouran; courtiers within and without all wished not to go, and Empress Dowager Bao also firmly stopped the emperor, but he would not listen.
idiomatic: In the second year of Shenjue the court debated attacking the Rouran. Ministers inside and out opposed the campaign, and Empress Dowager Bao also firmly dissuaded the emperor, but he would not listen.

literal: Only Hao approved it.
idiomatic: Only Hao supported it.

literal: Director of the Masters of Writing Liu Jie, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing An Yuan, and others had Yellow Gate Attendant Qiu Qi recommend Helian Chang's grand astrologer Zhang Shen and Xu Bian to tell the emperor: "This year is jisi, a year of triple yin; the Year Star assaults the moon and the White Star is in the west—arms must not be raised.
idiomatic: Director Liu Jie, Left Vice Director An Yuan, and others had Yellow Gate Attendant Qiu Qi bring forward Helian Chang's grand astrologer Zhang Shen and Xu Bian to tell the emperor, "This year is jisi, a year of triple yin. The Year Star assaults the moon and the White Star stands in the west—arms must not be raised."

literal: A northern campaign will surely fail; even if you conquer, it will not benefit the ruler."
idiomatic: "A northern campaign will fail; even victory will not benefit the throne."

literal: Moreover the ministers together praised Shen and the rest, saying: "In his youth Shen often admonished Fu Jian not to campaign south; Jian would not listen and was defeated.
idiomatic: The ministers together praised Shen and the others, saying, "In youth Shen often warned Fu Jian against a southern campaign. Jian would not listen and was defeated."

literal: Now the seasons, heaven, and human affairs are all out of harmony—how can you act?"
idiomatic: "Now heaven, the seasons, and human affairs are all out of harmony—how can we move?"

literal: The emperor was displeased and summoned Hao to debate with Shen and the rest.
idiomatic: The emperor was displeased and summoned Hao to debate Shen and the others.

literal: Hao refuted Shen, saying: "Yang is virtue and yin is punishment; therefore an eclipse of the moon means repairing punishment.
idiomatic: Hao refuted Shen: "Yang is virtue and yin is punishment, so a lunar eclipse means repairing punishment."

literal: When a king uses punishment, on a large scale he displays it in the wilds, on a small scale he exposes it in market and court.
idiomatic: "When a king uses punishment, on a grand scale he displays it in the wilds; on a small scale he exposes it in market and court."

literal: War is the greatest use of punishment.
idiomatic: "War is the greatest use of punishment."

literal: From this view, to use arms in a triple-yin year fits the category and the meaning of repairing punishment.
idiomatic: "From this view, using arms in a triple-yin year fits the category—it is the meaning of repairing punishment."

literal: The Year Star assaulting the moon means famine and people wandering—it applies to another state, twelve years distant.
idiomatic: "The Year Star assaulting the moon means famine and exodus—it applies to another state, twelve years hence."

literal: The White Star moving through the Azure Dragon lodges—in astronomy that is the east; it does not hinder a northern campaign.
idiomatic: "The White Star moving through the Azure Dragon lodges—in astronomy that is the east. It does not hinder a northern campaign."

literal: Shen and the rest are vulgar scholars, shallow in purpose and near in vision, dragged by numerology, not reaching the great body—hard to plan far with them.
idiomatic: "Shen and the rest are vulgar scholars, shallow in purpose and near in vision, dragged by numerology and unable to grasp the larger design—hard to plan far with them."

literal: Your servant observes the heavens: in recent years the moon's course has covered the Pleiades, and it is still so.
idiomatic: "I observe the heavens: in recent years the moon's course has covered the Pleiades, and it still does."

literal: Its omen: in three years the Son of Heaven will greatly break the Mao-tou country.
idiomatic: "Its omen: within three years the Son of Heaven will shatter the Mao-tou peoples."

literal: The Rouran and Gaoche are Mao-tou multitudes.
idiomatic: "The Rouran and Gaoche are Mao-tou peoples."

literal: When a sage illumines the age, he can perform extraordinary deeds.
idiomatic: "When a sage illumines the age, he can perform extraordinary deeds."

literal: The ancients said: 'At the source of the extraordinary, the people fear;
idiomatic: "The ancients said, 'At the source of the extraordinary the people fear;

literal: when it succeeds, all under heaven is tranquil.
idiomatic: 'when it succeeds, all under heaven is tranquil.'

literal: ' I beg Your Majesty not to doubt."
idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty not to doubt."

literal: Shen and the rest said in shame: "The Rouran are useless things beyond the wilds; gain their land and you cannot farm and eat, gain their people and you cannot make them subjects and use them.
idiomatic: Shen and the rest said shamefacedly, "The Rouran are useless folk beyond the wilds. Take their land and you cannot farm it; take their people and you cannot make them serve."

literal: Light and swift without constancy, hard to seize and control—why be so eager and weary horses and men?"
idiomatic: "They are light, swift, and unsteady—hard to seize and control. Why be so eager and weary horses and men?"

literal: Hao said: "Shen speaks of heaven's seasons—that is his office;
idiomatic: Hao said, "Shen speaks of heaven's seasons—that is his office."

literal: if one discusses situation and form, that is not what they know.
idiomatic: "If one discusses situation and form, that is not what they know."

literal: That is Han-era old talk and common saying; applied to today it does not fit the affairs of the time.
idiomatic: "That is Han-era platitude applied to today—it does not fit the affairs of the time."

literal: How so?
idiomatic: "How so?"

literal: The Rouran were formerly the state's northern border rebels and slaves; now execute their chief villains, gather their good men, and restore them to their old posts—not without use.
idiomatic: "The Rouran were once our northern border rebels and thralls. Execute their chief villains, gather their good men, restore them to their old posts—they are not useless."

literal: North of the desert it is high and cool, without gnats and mosquitoes; grass and water are fine; in summer they migrate north and pasture and farm the land—not impossible to farm and eat.
idiomatic: "North of the desert it is high and cool, free of gnats and mosquitoes, with fine grass and water. In summer they migrate north to pasture and farm—not land that cannot feed you."

literal: Rouran youths who come over are married to princesses if noble, made generals and grandees if humble, filling the court ranks.
idiomatic: "Rouran youths who surrender marry princesses if noble or become generals and grandees if humble—they fill the court ranks."

literal: Moreover the Gaoche are famed as named horsemen—not impossible to make subjects and keep.
idiomatic: "The Gaoche are famed horsemen—not impossible to make subjects and keep."

literal: If southerners pursue them, they fear their lightness and speed;
idiomatic: "If southerners pursue them, they fear their lightness and speed."

literal: with the state's troops it is not so.
idiomatic: "With the state's troops it is not so."

literal: How so?
idiomatic: "How so?"

literal: They can flee far; we can pursue far—not hard to control.
idiomatic: "They can flee far; we can pursue far—not hard to control."

literal: In past years they entered the passes many times and the people were shaken.
idiomatic: "In past years they raided the passes again and again and the people were shaken."

literal: If this summer you do not strike while they are open and advance to break and destroy their state, when autumn comes they will return and you cannot rest in peace.
idiomatic: "If this summer you do not strike while they are exposed and destroy their state, they will return in autumn and you cannot rest in peace."

literal: From the era of Emperor Taizong down to today there has been no year without alarm—is that not eager?
idiomatic: "From Emperor Taizong's day to now there has been no year without alarm—is that not urgent?"

literal: The world all says Shen and Bian understand numerology and clearly decide success and failure; your servant asks to test them.
idiomatic: "The world says Shen and Bian master numerology and judge success and failure. I ask to test them."

literal: Ask what signs of ruin their western state had before it was destroyed.
idiomatic: "Ask what signs of ruin their western state showed before it fell."

literal: If they knew and did not speak, that is disloyalty;
idiomatic: "If they knew and did not speak, that is disloyalty."

literal: if they truly did not know, that is lack of skill."
idiomatic: "If they truly did not know, that is lack of skill."

literal: Helian Chang was present; Shen and the rest, knowing they had no prior warning, were ashamed and could not reply.
idiomatic: Helian Chang was present. Shen and the rest, knowing they had given no prior warning, were ashamed and could not answer.

literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and said to the ministers: "My mind is decided.
idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased and told the ministers, "My mind is made up."

literal: One cannot plot with ministers of a destroyed state—how true!"
idiomatic: "One cannot plot with ministers of a destroyed state—how true!"

literal: Yet Empress Dowager Bao still doubted.
idiomatic: Yet Empress Dowager Bao still doubted.

literal: She again had the ministers debate before the empress dowager; the emperor ordered Hao to explain well and awaken her.
idiomatic: She had the ministers debate again before the empress dowager, and the emperor ordered Hao to explain matters clearly and win her over.

literal: When court ended, some blamed Hao, saying: "Wu bandits invade the south yet you leave that and campaign north—a host marching a thousand li, who does not know?"
idiomatic: When court ended, some blamed Hao: "Wu bandits invade the south, yet you leave that and march north—a host a thousand li on the road, who does not know it?"
